items.title: John Batiste "Bat" Stecklet Interview, 1959-06-15
items.q: he used to lead a concert band I heard his band when I was a boy

ctx.x: we'll play it for you but the other fellows in the band paint their part sometimes put in variations

yeah yeah yeah I used to play the whole lances and varieties through and through myself and you'd be the only one with the music with the melody you see and these other fellows would be doing the best they could and the guitar player or the bass player he'd follow the time now you asked me something about marches it's been my experience about marches that this fella John Philip Sousa he was the finest composer of six eight-ton marches of any man that I ever heard wrote music John Philip Sousa I know there was…
so we're just about through with this tape if there's any other question if not I think we've covered the your life pretty well and we certainly enjoyed talking to you hearing about those old times
